correctness.rationale: Dean words over 0,1,2,3 are squarefree with no adjacent inverse pairs 02,20,13,31. For fixed forbidden adjacent 10 the language is factorial. A complete independent direct-prefix enumeration, rescanning all substrings for every square at every extension and inverse-adjacencies, exactly reproduced all 60 survivor counts for n=0..59, with counts n54..59=(7,6,6,4,1,0); unique n58 word matches the cited 58-character witness. Direct pair-set inspection shows it misses only 10. The eight permutations commuting with alphabet inversion act transitively on the eight allowable length2 factors, therefore its eight distinct images are precisely all 58-long words missing any one allowable length2 pair. No extrapolation beyond this exhaustive finite boundary.

originality.rationale: Badkobeh–Harju–Ochem–Rosenfeld (2022) already prove the sharp maximum 58 for words avoiding 10 and print the same single witness, and infer every Dean word length≥59 has all allowable length-two pairs. Inspection of their full primary paper reveals no explicit fixed-pair uniqueness theorem nor classification of all length58 equality words. Thus the maximum 58, witness, and n59 consequence are not claimed original; uniqueness and one eight-element equality orbit are assessed best of knowledge, with authors’ unpublished backtracking data an acknowledged priority risk.
